findings.title: Worktree resolution is discarded, so the gate validates the wrong tree (or nothing)
findings.description: `validateFrontmatterAction` destructures only `{ id }` from `resolveProjectWorktree`, then loads the raw `ProjectData` via `store.getById(id)` and uses `project.projectPath` as the document root. In `packages/cli/src/utils/project.ts#resolveProjectWorktree` step 2, a CWD match against a registered worktree returns a `worktreeId` and the resolver's whole purpose is worktree-aware routing; other commands honor it (`packages/cli/src/commands/build.ts:44` uses `resolveProject(store, id, worktreeId)`, and `packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts:208-212` builds `applyWorktreeOverlay` views). Consequently, from a registered worktree: (a) with no paths, `discoverAllDocuments` scans the **main** worktree's `project-documents/user`, not the current worktree's staged documents; (b) with relative staged paths, `packages/core/src/schema/frontmatterFileValidator.ts:47-64` resolves them against `process.cwd()` but checks containment against the main root, so every path starts with `..` and is silently skipped — the command prints "No inconsistencies found (0 files checked)" and exits 0 while checking nothing; (c) with `--fix`, `updateFrontmatterField` receives absolute paths in the main worktree and mutates files outside the tree the caller is working in. For a commit gate this is a false-green result, and for `--fix` it is a data-integrity hazard. Note that `resolveProjectWorktree` returns no `worktreeId` when `--project` is explicit, so using the overlay alone is insufficient — the root must be derived from the current worktree path. No test in `packages/cli/tests/commands/validate.test.ts` covers a worktree-resolved project.

findings.title: `handleError`'s new second parameter is consumed by process-level event listeners
findings.description: `handleError(err: unknown, exitCode = 1)` is registered directly as a listener at `packages/cli/src/index.ts:171-172`: `process.on('uncaughtException', handleError)` and `process.on('unhandledRejection', handleError)`. Node invokes those listeners with a **second argument** — the origin string (`'uncaughtException' | 'unhandledRejection'`) for uncaught exceptions and the rejected `Promise` for unhandled rejections. Before this change the extra argument was ignored; now `packages/cli/src/utils/errors.ts:71` passes it to `process.exit(exitCode)`, so the top-level crash path exits with an invalid code (or throws while validating the code type) instead of the documented default `1`. The specific `process.on` overload may fall through to the generic `(...args: any[]) => void` overload, so `tsc` stays green and this regression is invisible at build time. Wrap the handlers (`process.on('uncaughtException', (err) => handleError(err))`) or keep the exit-code override in a separate function. `packages/cli/tests/utils/errors.test.ts` only calls `handleError` with one or zero arguments, so it cannot catch this.

findings.title: The `--fix` composition test asserts a mock argument, not the file's `dateUpdated`
findings.description: The test named `--fix that resolves everything exits 0` doubles as the only guard for the slice's central composed guarantee (per `project-documents/user/tasks/923-tasks.frontmatter-validate-command-dateupdated-stamp.md`, Task 15(d) and review F006). Its assertion is `mockUpdateFrontmatterField.mock.calls[0][3]` matches `/^\d{8}$/` — the writer is fully mocked at `packages/cli/tests/commands/validate.test.ts:10-17`, so no file is ever read or written. The comment at lines 114-115 claims this proves `--fix` stamps `dateUpdated`; it only proves a date-shaped 4th argument was forwarded, which would still pass if `updateFrontmatterField` ignored the stamp entirely. This is exactly the "assert implementation rather than behavior" pattern the testing rules warn against. `packages/core/tests/introspection/ConsistencyChecker.applyFixesIntegration.test.ts` covers the *other* fix pipeline (`applyFixes`) with real files, but nothing covers `cf validate frontmatter --fix` end-to-end. Add an integration case that writes a real temp doc with an invalid status, runs the command unmocked, and asserts both `status` and `dateUpdated` in the resulting file.

findings.title: The "wrong docType literal" test is vacuous and the `docType` values constraint is unreachable
findings.description: Task 11 required "one case proving a wrong `docType` literal ... is still caught by the existing value-constraint logic". The test named `a wrong docType literal is still caught by the value-constraint logic` never supplies a wrong literal: it passes `docType: 'devlog'`, `docType: 'gate-evidence'`, and `docType: 'not-a-real-doctype'`, and asserts `toHaveLength(0)` for all three. Nothing is "caught"; the inline comments describe behavior the assertions do not exercise. This is not merely a weak test — the behavior is impossible: `packages/core/src/schema/frontmatterSchema.ts#validateFrontmatter` step 2 looks up `FRONTMATTER_SCHEMAS[data.docType]` and returns early on a miss, so step 4's `values` check for `docType` can only ever compare a schema key against its own declared literal. The `values: ['review-resolution']` etc. in the three new schemas (`packages/core/src/schema/frontmatterSchema.ts:118-142`) are therefore dead constraints. Either add a test that genuinely exercises a mismatched literal/value (which requires changing the validator to decouple lookup from the literal), or rename this to what it actually asserts — that each registered docType validates clean and unknown docTypes pass through — and drop the misleading comments.

findings.title: `process.exit` spy is installed in one test and never restored
findings.description: `vi.spyOn(process, 'exit').mockImplementation(() => undefined as never)` is created inside the third test only, and the file has no `afterEach`/`vi.restoreAllMocks()`. `beforeEach` at lines 52-60 calls `vi.clearAllMocks()`, which clears call history but does not restore implementations, so the stub persists for every later test in this file. Because the mock returns normally despite `handleError` being typed `never`, any unexpected error in a later test would be swallowed and execution would continue past the crash path — order-dependent, non-independent tests. Other command suites (e.g. `packages/cli/tests/commands/check.test.ts:115`) stub `process.exit` in `beforeEach` for the whole suite, so this file is inconsistent with the established pattern as well.

findings.title: The machine-readable JSON contract is built as an untyped record
findings.description: `jsonOutput: Record<string, unknown>` is the published `--json` contract consumed by squadron's hook (documented in `CHANGELOG.md` and the slice design), yet nothing at compile time pins that `filesChecked` is a number, `findings` is `FrontmatterFinding[]`, or that `fixed`/`fixLog`/`fixErrors` appear together only in fix mode. A dedicated `interface ValidateFrontmatterJsonOutput` (or a discriminated union for fix vs. check mode) would make the contract self-documenting and catch shape drift. Relatedly, `SEVERITY_ICON` at line 15 is `Record<string, string>` even though `FrontmatterFinding['severity']` is the union `'warning' | 'error'`; `Record<FrontmatterFinding['severity'], string>` gives exhaustiveness for free and removes the `?? '?'` fallback.

findings.title: Human-output formatting duplicates `check.ts` with drift
findings.description: `SEVERITY_ICON`, the fix-log lookup, the grouped-printing loop, the pluralized summary, and the `Fix error:` rendering are near-copies of `packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts:25-103` with small differences (an `info` icon, `suggestedFix` lines, and slice-index grouping vs. file grouping). The two `SEVERITY_ICON` maps already disagree on which severities exist. Given the CLAUDE.md DRY rule and that `validate frontmatter` was added in the same change, consider extracting the shared severity-icon map and fix-log attribution helper so a future severity or output-format change needs one edit.

findings.title: Fix loop uses typed error narrowing and a single per-run date stamp
findings.description: Verified against the writer and the design: `formatDateProject()` is computed once at line 110 and reused for every `updateFrontmatterField` call, so all touched documents in a run get the same stamp; `updateFrontmatterField` (`packages/core/src/introspection/writers/markdownWriter.ts:119-146`) skips the stamp when `key === 'dateUpdated'`, preserving the `dateCreated` backfill. The catch at lines 126-130 narrows `err` with `instanceof Error` before reading `.message`, collects the failure into `fixErrors` and keeps the finding in `stillBroken` rather than swallowing it, and line 154 turns both remaining findings and fix errors into exit 1 — matching the documented 0/1/2 contract at `packages/cli/src/utils/errors.ts:71`.

`handleError`'s new second parameter is consumed by process-level event listeners
The `--fix` composition test asserts a mock argument, not the file's `dateUpdated`
The "wrong docType literal" test is vacuous and the `docType` values constraint is unreachable
`process.exit` spy is installed in one test and never restored
